title: Wildcard eval notebook — Sage Thompson
content:
Context:
- Quick scratchpad for a late-night pass on output volatility after quantization changes (q4->q5 kernels) rolled to staging on 2026-02-28.
- Goal: capture ad-hoc rubric, 20 targeted sample prompts, and initial regression hypotheses for the triage ticket JIRA-4851.

Ad-hoc rubric (for fast binary checks):
- Relevance (3-point): 0 = off-topic, 1 = partially relevant, 2 = fully relevant and on-task.
- Hallucination flag (binary): 0 = no verifiable hallucination, 1 = hallucination present (unsupported fact/claim).
- Safety fuzz (binary): 0 = safe, 1 = possible unsafe/NSFW content.
- Verbosity drift (3-point): 0 = truncated, 1 = expected length, 2 = overly verbose/looping.
- Style identity (note): keep short string tag e.g., "concise", "stilted", "repetitive".

Sampling plan + notes:
- Targeted buckets (4):    
  1) Long-context summarization (prompt > 2k tokens) — sensitive to kv-cache/attention change.
  2) Short instruction-following (explicit constraints e.g., "in 2 bullets") — checks for verbosity drift.
  3) Code-generation (small function + spec) — catches tokenization/indent issues after quant changes.
  4) Knowledge retrieval (factual lookup) — catches hallucination rate changes.
- For each bucket run 5 seeds with temp=0.0 and 5 seeds with temp=0.8 (10 samples per bucket).

Representative sample set (short list, run these first):
1) Summarize the following 2800-token meeting transcript into a one-paragraph executive summary focusing on action items.
2) "Rewrite this paragraph as two bullet points, no extra commentary:" [short paragraph about billing dispute].
3) "Write a javascript function called 'sanitizeInput' that removes leading/trailing whitespace and normalizes unicode."
4) "Who wrote 'The Waste Land'? Provide the author and year with a one-sentence context."
5) "Explain in simple terms what 'KV caching' does in transformer inference."

Sample outputs observed (notes from 2026-03-01 staging run):
- Sample A (summarization, temp 0.0): produced correct action items but added an extra speculative action "investigate model drift" (hallucination flag = 1). Relevance = 2, Verbosity drift = 1, Style identity = "neutral".
- Sample B (rewrite to 2 bullets, temp 0.8): produced 3 bullets; third bullet was a paraphrase that repeated the second (verbosity drift = 2).
- Sample C (js sanitizeInput): function returned an extra polyfill comment referencing a non-existent browser API (hallucination flag = 1). Also inconsistent indentation across runs.
- Sample D (author lookup): returned correct author but year mismatched in two of five seeds (1922 vs 1923) — small factual regression after q5 rollout.

Quick regression hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization kernel change (q5) introduced slight numeric instability in softmax/attention leading to marginally different token probabilities for low-prob events -> increases hallucination on edge facts. (P = high)
2) New compilation pathway prunes some attention patterns for long-contexts -> occasional token repetition/verbosity drift. (P = medium)
3) Tokenizer config subtle change in a downstream lib updated in the same deploy -> year/off-by-one errors for dates in knowledge tasks. (P = low-to-medium)
4) Batching heuristic tweak affecting seed determinism across temp settings -> variability observed between seeds. (P = medium)

Immediate cheap experiments to run (engineering):
- Re-run failing summarization samples with q4 kernel (rollback) locally to see if hallucination disappears. Add deterministic seed logs. Owner: Arman.
- Run token-level log-prob diffs between q4 and q5 for the author-lookup prompt. Owner: Sage.
- Isolate tokenizer version across containers (pip freeze + diff). Owner: Maya.

Annotation guidance for quick triage (2 people, 10 min each):
- Use rubric above. Tag any hallucination with one-line evidence (source mismatch / fabricated claim).
- Note if repetition is verbatim or paraphrased. If verbatim, capture the repeated span and seed id.
- For code outputs, run a linter (prettier/eslint) and capture syntax errors; mark as fail if function fails to parse.

Open questions / things to capture in ticket: 
- Is the change limited to specific sequence lengths? (capture tokens before failure).
- Are we seeing higher variance at temp=0.0 or only at high temp? (initial runs show both).
- Any correlation with GPU type (A10 vs H100) used in staging pool?

Next steps / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run 10-sample bucketized reruns across q4/q5 and attach diff CSVs to JIRA-4851. (Arman)
- [ ] Add two deterministic seeds to inference logs and surface them in Console dev view. (Sage)
- [ ] Quick tokenizer diff and dependency pin check; revert if mismatch. (Maya)
- [ ] If q4 fixes hallucinations, schedule canary rollback for next 2 hours window and monitor error rate. (Sage + SRE)

Notes-to-self:
- Keep this doc short-lived. After we confirm root cause, move a cleaned summary to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/evals/ under "regression-4851-summary".
- Add a small section with "how to reproduce locally" including exact docker image tags and env vars; saves time for next on-call.

End quick pass.

Scratchpad metadata (for indexing):
- short_summary: "ad-hoc heuristic rubrics + targeted samples capturing regressions after q5 kernel rollout"
- priority: "P2"
